summary: Per-frame vehicle physics integration driver on the vehicle object: saves/restores the FPU control word, runs the main physics update, then executes a sub-stepped (RK2 midpoint) integration loop over the accumulated timestep with wheel-data copies, force accumulation per wheel block, collision-damage/DNF detection across four collision bodies, and inertia-tensor world-space transforms for four wheel-link sub-objects. Gated at entry by a physics-override double and an enable byte.

local_names.v19/v29: used / remaining sub-step time within the integration loop
local_names.v10: wheel-link sub-object block cursor (strided by 1124 bytes from this+0x310)
local_names.v11: collision sub-object pointer read at this+0x3EC
local_names.v12: world-space matrix object pointer read at this+0x15F0

operations.description: Entry gate: when the physics-override double at 0x005D6D70 equals 1.0, or the enable byte at 0x007CE254 is zero, the entire per-frame physics step is skipped (early return).
Save the FPU control word via FPUControlWordMaskExtract(512); the saved value is restored at function exit.
Run VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate(this) before the sub-stepped integration loop.

Sub-step integration loop: starts with i = the timestep field this+0x68 (as double), and repeats while the accumulated time v29 remains greater than the used time v19, feeding i = v29 - v19 into each iteration. The accumulator this+0x60 is read and advanced within the body.

Midpoint integration of one sub-step: PhysicsIntegrationStep(this); WheelDataCopy(this, i*0.5); advance the accumulator this+0x60 by the half-step; PhysicsIntegrationStep(this) again; then PhysicsStepFrame(this, v19) finalizes the frame.

Sub-step remainder handling: when the accumulator v5 is below 1.0 and dword_7CE958 is set with v19 differing from the dt field this+0x68, rescale v5 by dt/v19; when still below 1.0, compute a capped remainder (v5 <= 0.5 ? v19 = v5*0.999*v19 : v19 = half-step), flooring v19 at 0.000003814697265625.

Remainder sub-step pass: StateAccumulateDelta(this); WheelDataCopy(this, v19*0.5); reset the accumulator this+0x60 to v19*0.5 plus the pre-loop value; PhysicsIntegrationStep(this); PhysicsStepFrame(this, v19).
Post-loop commit: store this+0x1658 = this+0x844 + this+0x3E0; then reset the accumulator this+0x60 to the frame-delta argument a2.
Run EngineStressSimulation(this) after the integration loop.

Per-wheel force accumulation: iterate four wheel blocks strided by 1124 bytes anchored at this+0x338; for each, read the double value, dispatch it via InterruptDispatch, write it back, then call VehicleDynamicsForceAccumulatorIntegration(block-172, dt-from-this+0x68).

Collision damage / DNF detection across the four strided collision-body anchors, each call taking the dt field this+0x68 and a count/argument read from the enumerated pointer fields this+0x3EC, this+0x850, this+0x141C, and (on the conditional branch) this+0xCB4 / this+0x1118.

Inertia-transform loop over four wheel-link blocks strided by 1124 bytes anchored at this+0x310: for each block read the collision sub-object pointer at this+0x3EC; when present and its active flag this+0x450 is clear, load the sub-object velocity components (fields *(this+0x3EC)+0x1C/+0x34/+0x4C) and the wheel-link vectors at this+0x310/0x318, combine them with the world-space matrix rows of the this+0x15F0 object (fields 0x4..0x5C), and guard the transform on the computed dot (skip when below 0.5 or the second dot exceeds 0.7).

Apply the transform: call sub_56BDE0(block+16, 0); copy the computed 0x18-byte position block into the sub-object; call F_3x3InertiaTensorTransform(subobj); copy the 0x18-byte matrix block; call InertiaTensorWorldSpaceTransform(subobj); then PhysicsSubObjectFree(this).
Restore the FPU control word: when the saved value differs from 512 call EmptyStub_7780(saved); otherwise return the earlier result value.

clean_pseudocode: for (4 wheel blocks strided 1124 from this+0x338): InterruptDispatch(value); VehicleDynamicsForceAccumulatorIntegration(block-172, dt);
PhysicsCollisionDamageDNFDetection over four collision bodies with dt and the this+0x3EC/0x850/0x141C/0xCB4/0x1118 counts;
for (4 wheel-link blocks strided 1124 from this+0x310):
read velocity *(this+0x3EC)+0x1C/0x34/0x4C and matrix this+0x15F0 rows 0x4..0x5C;
if (dot ok) { sub_56BDE0(block+16, 0); copy position; F_3x3InertiaTensorTransform(subobj); copy matrix; InertiaTensorWorldSpaceTransform(subobj); PhysicsSubObjectFree(this); }

The collision-body anchors (four bodies) and the wheel/wheel-link block addresses beyond the enumerated anchor fields are derived by 1124-byte stride and are not individually enumerated among the packet fields.

The sub-object fields written by the qmemcpy calls (offsets +4, +28, +124 inside the this+0x3EC object) and the matrix object field at this[1404]+124 are not enumerated among the packet fields; their roles are DERIVED.
The literal 0.7 and 0.5 thresholds in the inertia-transform guard have DERIVED semantics only.
